A stock just paid for my new fridge. Thirty five thousand rupees, and zero from my savings. Here's how you can plan yours.
My rule is simple. Write down what I need, add twenty percent for tax, and let a stock earn it.
The stock I picked was Cupid. Three hundred and sixty seven shares, at an average price of two hundred and twenty four rupees.
Today it trades at three fifty three. My eighty two thousand rupees is now worth one lakh, twenty nine thousand.
That's a profit of forty seven thousand, more than my target. Selling about one hundred and seven shares covers the fridge, even after tax.
So the stock bought our fridge. And two hundred and sixty shares are still working for me.
But remember. Profit on screen is not money in hand. Small caps can fall just as fast. Follow for the next real P and L.
